holding_entity: Leaguer Telecom (Hong Kong); Hongkong Everfine Investment
summary: Anatolia Telekom announced a Chinese-partnered domestic phone to be produced in Erzincan (2010).
Dardanel's capital rose from 34.8m to 85m TL with shares allotted to an ADM Capital–Yıldız vehicle (2011).

project_name: CNR investment in Malatya wagon repair factory
summary: Malatya governor signed a goodwill agreement with China's CNR (2012).

Chery's Turkish distributor Mermerler Otomotiv repeatedly announced a 500–550m USD car plant in Sakarya (Karasu/Adapazarı) from 2008 to 2011; the archive shows delays and site/permit issues but no production start.

Hong Kong-listed China Hengshi announced in June 2018 that it had set up Hengshi Turkey to make fiberglass fabrics for wind blades, with a designed capacity of about 10,000 t a year. The source is a stock-exchange announcement; no press report on the plant was found.
Minister Çağlayan said in 2009 a Chinese automaker would build a plant with a Turkish partner, possibly in Konya.

project_name: Chinese/HK investors in Ağaoğlu Bodrum project
investor: Chinese construction group; HK financial investor
summary: Ağaoğlu signed a preliminary agreement with a Chinese construction group and a Hong Kong investor for its Bodrum tourism city (2017).
The Investment Support Agency announced a 250m USD DFM plant (52,000 vehicles/yr, 1,000 jobs) in 2009; no later evidence of construction.

EVE Energy's subsidiary and Aksa Jeneratör signed a memorandum of understanding in January 2024 to set up a joint venture in Turkey making battery modules, cabinets and containers and building storage projects. Shares, site and amount were left to a final agreement, which has not been reported.

Yiğit Akü disclosed in August 2024 a framework agreement with Ganfeng's battery arm for a 500m USD joint venture: a 5 GWh lithium cell and pack plant with R&D centres and about 400 staff on a 132,000 m² plot, to apply under the HIT-30 programme. The site has not been disclosed and no later progress has been reported.

status_detail: Joint venture signed (May 2024); venture company set up (2025)
summary: Altek Alarko (60%) and Gotion's Singapore company (40%) signed a joint venture agreement in May 2024 for a storage-system assembly plant followed by lithium-ion cell production in Turkey. A September 2026 column says the venture company was set up in 2025 and targets about 600 jobs and exports to 69 countries; a round-up put the expected investment at about 300m USD. The site is not reported.
H3C opened a Turkey office, signed distribution with Boğaziçi Bilgisayar (2020) and in 2021 was deciding on a factory in the Marmara region (about 50m USD, 200 jobs at first and 1,200 targeted).

Hanergy agreed with Çankırı officials in June 2017 on a panel factory (about 500 jobs) and a 300 MW energy park at Yakınkent OSB, on a 480 ha site; a good-faith certificate was signed and the company asked for six months of preparation. No amount was given and no later report was found.
Harbin Electric and Hattat's HEMA signed a 250m USD, 50-50 JV to make power-plant equipment, targeting 2,000 jobs (2012).

investment_type: Cell factory with Chinese partner (equity not disclosed)
summary: Schmid Pekintaş announced in June 2025 a 5 GW TOPCon solar cell factory in Düzce with the Chinese firm JTPV under the HIT-30 programme, with groundbreaking in 2025 and production in 2026. Headlines call it a Chinese–Turkish partnership, but one report describes JTPV as the technology supplier and no shareholding is given.

investor: Kaishan Group (OME Eurasia); with Transmark Renewables
status_detail: Joint venture agreed (October 2022); completion not confirmed
summary: In October 2022 Transmark Renewables and Kaishan agreed that Kaishan's subsidiary would put up to 21m USD into the company running the Gülpınar geothermal plant for 49% of its shares, to fund a 15.8 MW expansion budgeted at 58m USD with Kaishan supplying the power units. Whether the stake was taken up and the expansion finished is not reported.

project_name: Li & Fung textile project in Southeastern Anatolia
summary: Li & Fung said in 2008 it planned to revive idle textile capacity in the GAP region with Arslan Group.
A sector article said LiuGong had decided to invest in Turkey's construction-machinery sector (2014).

project_name: SANY and three other Chinese firms near investment decision
summary: Minister Ergün said in 2010 that SANY and three other Chinese firms were about to decide on investments.

project_name: SDIC wind farms (Aydın and Manisa, 170 MW)
status_detail: MoU signed (2018); no later reports found
summary: China's state investor SDIC (80%) and Smart Growth Holding (20%) signed a 226m USD MoU in 2018 to take over the 30 MW Söke wind farm and build four licensed wind farms (140 MW), with PowerChina as contractor.

status_detail: Talks with SPIC (2024); no final agreement by September 2026
summary: EÜAŞ, Westinghouse and China's SNPTC signed an MoU in 2014 for a third nuclear plant (İğneada); talks continued to 2019.

Skyworth and Ulubaşlar Group's Ulu Motor agreed in June 2023 on a 25m USD battery module and pack plant in Turkey, planned for early 2024, with a vehicle line to follow; the Turkish partner later spoke of a 1.6bn USD plan. In October 2024 the vehicle line was still described as a plan, and no opening has been reported.

status_detail: Investment decision announced (2019); completion not reported
summary: Representatives of China's TTX Group said in June 2019 that they would build a kitchen equipment factory in the Çilimli organised industrial zone employing 300 people, with a start planned for November 2019.

project_name: Tiron–Ekin Makina wind turbine parts plant (Uzunköprü)
summary: The Chinese firm Tiron and Ekin Makina received land in the Atatürk organised industrial zone in Uzunköprü in May 2025 to build a factory for wind turbine parts for the domestic and export markets; the Chinese firm is to move its European production to Turkey.

investor: Ant International; Trendyol (Alibaba); with Baykar and ADQ
summary: Trendyol, Baykar, Abu Dhabi's ADQ and Ant International signed a memorandum in July 2025 to set up a fintech platform in Turkey offering payments, loans, deposits, investment products and insurance. Stakes and amounts were not disclosed and the launch has not been reported.

project_name: Tufanbeyli lignite power plant (TEYO and Chinese partner)
summary: TEYO and its Chinese partner signed a 30-year royalty deal for a 600 MW, 1.2bn USD plant at Tufanbeyli (2012).

project_name: Turkish–Chinese industrial park in Niğde Bor
summary: Plans for ~200 Chinese factories and 15,000 jobs at Bor OSB were reported in 2012.
A sector article said XCMG had decided to invest in Turkey's construction-machinery sector (2014).

investor: Yongjin Technology Group (80%); two Chinese partners
summary: Yongjin Technology Group announced in March 2025 a cold-rolled stainless steel plant of 400,000 t a year in the Yalova Makine İhtisas organised industrial zone, reported at 257m USD (250m USD in some reports), through a venture in which it holds 80% and two other Chinese firms 15% and 5%. Construction was to take about 24 months; no report of its start was found.

investor: ZS Türkiye Automotive Spare Parts (Chinese parent not named)
summary: The Investment Office reported in January 2026 that ZS Türkiye Automotive Spare Parts signed a land allocation agreement for a 116,000 m² auto parts facility in the İpsala and Uzunköprü organised industrial zones, expected to create 1,660 jobs. The Chinese parent and the amount are not given.

project_name: Zhejiang Energy–Polat coal mine & power plant (Soma)
summary: A protocol for a >1bn USD coal mine and power plant in Soma/Kınık was signed in 2011, billed as the first big Chinese FDI.

status_detail: Preliminary agreement – not realised in archive
summary: Zorlu and China's GSR Capital signed a preliminary agreement in February 2018 for 4.5bn USD of investment by 2023: a 25 GW-a-year battery plant and nickel and cobalt processing, at Gördes (Manisa) and Eskişehir, as 50-50 partnerships with 4,000 jobs. No later report of its realisation was found.

project_name: AVIC EPC framework for Hattat Amasra plant
summary: Contractor role (1bn USD EPC framework, 2012).

project_name: Aksa Enerji hydropower plants (7 plants, 251 MW)
summary: Aksa Enerji and CNTIC agreed in 2013 to build seven hydropower plants for USD 463m, mostly financed by Chinese lenders.

investor: CRCC (CCECC); CMC (with Cengiz and IC İçtaş)
summary: A consortium of CRCC and CMC with Cengiz and IC İçtaş won the second stage of the Ankara–Istanbul high-speed line in 2005 with Chinese credit; the 1.27bn USD section, of which 720m USD Chinese loans, opened in July 2014.

Chinese contractors CPI Power Engineering and AVIC International built Diler Holding's 2×600 MW Atlas coal-fired plant at İskenderun, in commercial operation from late 2014; CPI Power Engineering has operated and maintained it since 2015.
700m USD coal extraction contract (2013).

project_name: Chinese firms in Mersin rail finance-and-build talks
summary: Preliminary talks (2019).
Government-to-government talks for a faster Ankara–Istanbul line (2013).

project_name: Chinese technology/EPC for Eti Maden boron carbide plant
summary: Eti Maden's boron carbide plant uses Dalian Jinma technology and is built by CMEC; the plant is state-owned.
Contractor role in Hattat's Amasra coal mining (2012).

project_name: Gezhouba EPC for Eğirdir pumped hydro
summary: 1.5bn USD EPC contract with KAF for a 1,000 MW pumped-storage plant (2020).

project_name: ICBC loan for Ciner's Ilgın power plant (Konya)
summary: Ciner Group signed a 13-year, 508m USD loan package with ICBC in May 2015 for a 500 MW coal-fired plant at Ilgın, Konya, with a total investment of about 700m USD and generation planned for 2019. No report of the plant's completion was found.
CETC agreed in 2019 to supply and install the equipment for Kalyon's 400m USD integrated solar panel factory in Ankara (500 MW a year, about 1,500 jobs).
China Tianchen Engineering built Ciner's Kazan natural soda ash and power complex, financed by Chinese banks (2013 agreement); no Chinese equity stake was reported.

project_name: Kontrolmatik battery storage and wind project (Tekirdağ)
summary: Harbin Electric International agreed about USD 300m for a Kontrolmatik 1 GWh storage plant with a 250 MW wind farm (2024).
Sinoma signed a turnkey EPC contract with Limak in 2015 for a 5,000 tpd cement plant in Polatlı, 85% financed by a Chinese export-credit-insured loan.
Sinoma signed a USD 780m agreement with Eren Holding in 2010 for two cement lines near Mersin; the plant opened in 2015 with one line.

Sinopec Oilfield Service said in May 2017 that its Turkish unit signed an 84.6m USD, 30-month contract with GCL ND to drill 26 geothermal wells; the report does not give the location. GCL ND is itself a venture of China's GCL group and is recorded as a separate project.

investor: China Tianchen Engineering (CNCEC); China CAMC Engineering; ICBC
summary: BOTAŞ chose China Tianchen in 2011 to build the Tuz Gölü salt-cavern gas storage (USD 640m); in 2018 ICBC signed a USD 1.2bn loan MoU for the Tuz Gölü and Silivri expansions. The phase II expansion (from 2019) is being built by China CAMC Engineering with IC İçtaş.
A Sinoma design institute won the engineering and procurement contract for a new Votorantim Çimento line (2015).
CMEC built the two 600 MW units of Eren Enerji's ZETES coal complex under a 2007 EPC contract.

project_name: Zhejiang Orient agreement for Umutlu HES
summary: Agreement for a 21.5 MW hydro plant; the Chinese role is not stated (likely EPC).
European Nickel lined up Chinese offtake and about USD 350m of Chinese debt for Çaldağ with China Tianchen as contractor (2009); the project stalled.

project_name: ADM Capital partnership in Işıklar Holding
summary: ADM Capital partnered with Işıklar Holding from about 2006 and exited in January 2012.

project_name: Akkuyu nuclear tender – Chinese spec buyer (2008)
summary: A Chinese company bought the 2008 Akkuyu tender documents but did not submit a bid.

status_detail: Agreed July 2024; BYD put it on hold (June 2026); ministry starting legal steps to recover incentives and land
summary: Turkey and BYD agreed in July 2024 on a 1bn USD plant in Manisa for 150,000 electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles a year, with an R&D centre and about 5,000 jobs. An environmental application was filed in October 2024, but the site stayed empty through 2025. In June 2026 BYD's Stella Li said the project was on hold with no timeline; the ministry said BYD's obligations and guarantees remain valid, and in July 2026 the minister told parliament that legal steps to cancel incentives, call guarantees and take back the land were starting.

project_name: CRBC in the 1915 Çanakkale Bridge tender
investor: China Road and Bridge Corp (with Cengiz–Kolin)
summary: CRBC bid with Cengiz and Kolin for the bridge BOT in 2017; the Daelim–Limak–SK–Yapı Merkezi group won.

project_name: China Sunergy (CSUN) solar module factory, Tuzla
status_detail: Opened 2013 (120 MW, Tuzla Free Zone); production halted 2018
summary: China Sunergy announced a 600m USD panel factory with Seul Enerji in 2012 and opened a 120 MW module plant in the Tuzla Free Zone in 2013; the plant grew until 2017, and in 2018 production stopped with workers' wages unpaid.

project_name: China's bid for the Sinop nuclear plant
summary: China negotiated for Turkey's second nuclear plant in Sinop in 2012–13; the project went to the Japanese–French consortium.
amount_reported: 20,000–22,000m USD (whole plant; not a Chinese stake)

project_name: Chinese bidders in Karapınar YEKA solar
summary: Two consortia with Chinese members bid in the 2017 1,000 MW Karapınar YEKA; Kalyon–Hanwha won.

project_name: Chinese stake in Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge & North Marmara Motorway
investor: China Merchants Expressway; Jiangsu Expressway; Zhejiang Expressway
summary: A Chinese consortium agreed in Dec 2019 to buy 51% of the bridge operator ICA for about 659–689m USD; in Aug 2021 IC Holding suspended talks pending refinancing.
STFA bid for Başkent Gaz with China's ENN via a 50-50 company (2012); the archive does not show them winning.

project_name: Goldwind and MingYang in YEKA wind tender
summary: Goldwind (with Akfen–Beyçelik) and MingYang bid in the 1,000 MW wind YEKA (2017) but did not win.

Great Wall was reported in July 2023 to be in advanced talks with the Investment Office, with the Manisa land once reserved for Volkswagen proposed as the site. In February 2024 it was reported to have suspended the plan, citing rising costs and frequently changing regulations.

Chongqing-based Lifan set up a motorcycle assembly plant in Çilimli, Düzce (24,000 m² site), announced in December 2007 with production from April 2008; in 2009 it was assembling one motorcycle every 20 minutes, largely from Chinese parts. The Turkish company has since been struck off the trade registry.

status_detail: Own production suspended (January 2023) and reported closed (May 2023); made by Turkish partner AGM at Tuzla since 2024
summary: OPPO opened a smartphone plant in Tuzla in 2021 (reported at 50m USD). Production stopped at the turn of 2023 and in May 2023 the plant was reported closed, with production moving to Egypt. In January 2024 OPPO signed a partnership under which the Turkish firm AGM (Mıstaçoğlu Holding) makes OPPO phones at the Tuzla site.

MG's Turkish distributor said in May 2023 that SAIC had shelved an advanced plant plan after Turkey's 40% additional duty on Chinese electric cars; in 2024 he said talks had revived and reached the letter-of-intent stage. In June 2026 MG was reported to have chosen Galicia, Spain, for its first European plant. All statements on the Turkish plan come from the distributor.
The Hong Kong chain entered via Bursa's Çelik Palas in 2015 and left in 2017.
Hong Kong's Hutchison was in the Global–Hutchison–EİB consortium that won İzmir Port's 49-year concession for 1.275bn USD in 2007; after court delays the consortium did not take over the port.
BYD said in 2014 it was studying Turkey as a production base for electric buses.

project_name: Beylikova rare earths cooperation with China
summary: Turkey signed a memorandum with China in October 2024 on the Beylikova rare earth reserve. A year later, Turkish outlets citing Bloomberg reported that the talks had stalled because China wanted the ore processed in China while Turkey insisted on domestic refining and technology transfer, and that Turkey had opened talks with the United States.
Mainly an EPC contractor, CMEC said in 2013 it was eyeing electricity distribution.

status_detail: Announced by Turkish officials (March 2025); Chery says no decision (2026); site empty
summary: Chery said in 2023 it was studying production in Turkey, and in 2024 the minister said talks were in their final chapters. In March 2025 Turkish officials announced a 1bn USD plant in Samsun for 200,000 vehicles a year with over 5,000 jobs, while Chery told Reuters it had no plan to build a factory and sought a third-party partnership. In 2026 its Turkish executive said no decision had been taken; the allocated plot was reported empty in April 2026.

project_name: Chinese bid for the Afşin-Elbistan coal complex
summary: Turkey negotiated a 10–12bn USD Afşin-Elbistan deal with China in 2013–16; no agreement is reported.
Reports of Chinese investors forming partnerships for coal exploration (Manisa) and chrome deposits (Erdemli).

project_name: Chinese construction investment feasibility in Van
summary: A Chinese firm with a local partner set aside 12m TL for a feasibility study in Van (2012).

project_name: Chinese interest in Istanbul's third airport
summary: Minister Yıldırım listed Chinese firms among those interested in the third-airport tender (2012).
Officials held preliminary talks with Chinese firms on Kanal İstanbul (2014-15).

project_name: Chinese interest in a 1,320 MW coal plant
summary: The EPDK head said Chinese firms wanted to build a 1,320 MW coal plant and other energy assets (2015).

project_name: Chinese partners in Humartaş renewable projects
summary: Humartaş said it runs joint projects with Chinese firms and that panel makers provide funding (2015).

status_detail: Plan announced by Turkish association (September 2022); no follow-up
summary: After about 100 executives of Chinese promotional-products firms visited Turkey, the sector association PROMOTÜRK said in September 2022 that they would set up three factories in less-developed provinces from early 2023 with at least 10,000 jobs. No company, province or later report was found.

project_name: Chinese renewable firms seeking land in Silifke
summary: Silifke OSB received land requests from Chinese renewable-energy firms but could not meet them (2014).

project_name: Chinese wind blade factory (Çine or Bandırma)
summary: Late-July 2026 reports say an unnamed Chinese wind turbine maker is choosing between the Çine (Aydın) and Bandırma (Balıkesir) organised industrial zones for a blade factory of about 300m EUR and more than 125,000 m², with about 600 jobs. A decision was expected by the end of August 2026; the outcome has not been reported.

Energy minister Bayraktar said in September 2025 that he discussed with Dongfang Electric its plan for a wind turbine factory in Turkey with 2,000 MW annual capacity and an initial investment of about 250m USD.

Dongfeng's Turkish distributor Marcar said in January 2026 that talks were under way to build the Voyah Free REV 318 in Turkey with an unnamed investor that has secured a production facility, aiming to start in 2026. A July 2026 report places the plan in Kocaeli and says feasibility work continues.

project_name: Geely investment plan with Anadolu Group
summary: ISPAT listed Geely as planning investment in Turkey with Anadolu Group (2010).

project_name: Hisense production plan with Anadolu Group
summary: Hisense entered the market via Anadolu Group's Antek and said it wanted a Turkish production facility (2010).
JAC said in 2011 it wanted to invest in Turkey, especially in EVs.
The Chinese linen yarn maker said a factory and flax growing in Turkey could be studied (2012).

project_name: Luoyang Yizong halal food partnership idea
summary: The Chinese halal meat producer said in 2012 it was considering a Turkish partnership and its own supermarket chain.

project_name: MİA Teknoloji–Dynalion e-bike and battery plan
investor: Suzhou Dynalion Technology; with MİA Teknoloji
summary: MİA Teknoloji told the stock exchange in February 2025 that its subsidiary signed a memorandum with China's Suzhou Dynalion Technology for a joint investment in Turkey in shared electric bicycles and battery production, and had begun feasibility work for a plant. Site and amount were not disclosed.
Risen Solar sent a team to Van for a solar-investment feasibility study (2014).

project_name: Senstone Capital tourism and food investments
summary: Senstone Capital said in 2018 it would invest 150m USD in Turkish tourism and food, naming the Grand Hyatt Istanbul among hotels it wanted to buy.
Seres Group's overseas president called Turkey the most important candidate country for a European production facility in July 2024. No site, amount or later step has been reported.

project_name: Shenhua–DEI bid for Eskişehir thermal plant
summary: Greece's DEI said it bid with Shenhua for an Eskişehir thermal plant (2018).
Sinotruk visited in 2014 to explore production and trade options.

project_name: Sinovel turbine supply and localisation invitation
summary: Ağaoğlu agreed to buy turbines for 600 MW and invited Sinovel to produce components in Turkey (2012).
StarTimes said in 2017 it was preparing to invest and looking for a Turkish partner.
TBEA expressed interest in solar investment (2008) and gave PM Erdoğan an 'investment promise' in Urumqi (2012); no project followed in the archive.
Wetown Electric Group was reported in August 2024 to be studying factories in Denizli and Adana; its chairman visited the Denizli Chamber of Industry. No amount or later step has been reported.

State-owned Air China started Beijing–Istanbul flights on 29 December 2023 (three a week), becoming the fourth Chinese airline at Istanbul Airport; in 2026 it widened its codeshare with Turkish Airlines to all direct flights between the two countries.
Alibaba Cloud entered Turkey through a partnership with E-Glober (2018).
Alibaba.com entered Turkey through a local partnership (2011).

İş Bankası has accepted Alipay for e-commerce since 2017 and on physical POS since 2019; in May 2019 Alipay launched with ininal for Chinese tourists in Istanbul and Cappadocia, the year its Turkish company was registered.
BGI Genomics and Turkey's Genoks extended their partnership in 2018 to expand prenatal testing and sequencing services in Turkey.
Chinese-owned Benelli agreed with Kuba Motor to make Turkey its third production site, using Kuba's Gaziantep plant (2017).
China Eastern made its first Shanghai–Istanbul flight in late September 2023, flying three times a week, as the third Chinese carrier at Istanbul Airport after Sichuan Airlines and China Southern.

Pasifik Eurasia signed a container transport agreement with China Railway International Multimodal in June 2025 for China–Turkey–Europe freight on the Middle Corridor, starting with 10 block trains and targeting 1,000 a year.
China Southern flew Beijing/Urumqi–Istanbul from 2011, suspended in July 2016, returned in late 2018, resumed after the pandemic in June 2022 and launched Guangzhou–Istanbul in June 2024.

project_name: Chinese manufacturer partner in Reeder's Samsun plant
summary: Reeder said it set up its Samsun phone plant with support from its Chinese manufacturer, on EBRD advice to take a strategic partner (2018).

project_name: Hithium storage partnerships (Maxxen; Norm Yeşil Enerji)
summary: In 2024 the Chinese cell maker Hithium signed a letter of intent with Norm Yeşil Enerji for a 1 GWh container storage plant in Velimeşe, Tekirdağ, and an exclusive partnership with Maxxen covering storage manufacturing and its trademark in Turkey. No Chinese shareholding is reported in either.
Hong Kong-based hotel groups operate hotels in Istanbul and Bodrum; the articles describe brand/management roles, not ownership. The Shangri-La Bosphorus is recorded separately.

status_detail: Reported decision (September 2026); not confirmed by the company
summary: Several outlets reported in September 2026, citing unnamed sector sources, that Honor has decided to make smartphones in Avcılar, Istanbul, in cooperation with Salcomp. No amount, capacity or start date is given.

status_detail: Partnership signed (November 2023); production start not confirmed
summary: Huawei Türkiye and the Turkish firm EGS signed a partnership in November 2023 under which EGS makes solar inverters under the Partner EGS brand with Huawei's technical support. In May 2024 the Turkish firm said its Ankara factory would start in October 2024 with 2 GW a year and about 17m USD of its own investment.

project_name: JA Solar panels made by HSA Enerji (Manisa)
summary: HSA Enerji makes JA Solar panels alongside its own brand at its Manisa plant (500 MW in 2022, a second factory planned); trade press describes this as JA Solar's local OEM production.
İhlas Motor agreed with JAC to assemble 3.5-t LCVs in its Yalova plant (2012); no Chinese equity is reported.

Chinese rail firm Liyuan signed an agreement with state wagon maker TÜVASAŞ in 2018 to develop metro, tram and light-rail projects, saying joint ventures could follow; TÜVASAŞ had ordered 12 trains from it.

project_name: SWM and JAC kit assembly at Urzat (Eskişehir)
investor: SWM (Shineray); JAC; with Urzema Holding and ATMO Group
status_detail: SWM assembly started (December 2025); JAC to follow
summary: Urzat Otomotiv, a venture of ATMO Group and Urzema Holding, has assembled the SWM G01 Pro from imported kits in the Eskişehir organised industrial zone since December 2025, which avoids the 40% duty on Chinese-made cars; the electric JAC E30X is to follow on the same line. No equity by the Chinese makers is reported.
TCL began SKD phone production with Arçelik at Çerkezköy OSB in 2021 (450,000/yr); no Chinese equity is reported.
Trina Solar supplies modules to Turkish solar projects (a 40 MW deal with Tegnatia in 2016); press reports show supply contracts only, no plant.

project_name: Wanda Vista Istanbul hotel management (Mar Yapı)
summary: Wanda Hotels & Resorts signed with Mar Yapı in February 2017 to manage the 150-room Wanda Vista Istanbul, its first hotel outside China, then due to open at the end of 2018. Mar Yapı is the owner and investor.
ADM Capital is listed among funds that entered the Turkish health sector (2014).

project_name: ADM Capital stake in STFA Yatırım Holding
summary: A 2008 article reports that 21% of STFA Yatırım Holding was sold to Hong Kong-based ADM Capital.

Alibaba took control of Trendyol through share purchases and capital increases and had invested 1.4bn USD by 2023. In September 2023 its president told President Erdoğan that Alibaba would invest a further 2bn USD, with a data centre in Ankara and an export centre at Istanbul Airport planned; no report of their completion was found. In May 2025 Trendyol agreed to sell 85% of its delivery unit Trendyol Go to Uber for about 700m USD.
amount_reported: 350m USD (2021 capital increase; 2018 deal value not in archive)

summary: Reports on Astronergy's Balıkesir project say the company already runs a solar panel factory in Adana with 1 GW annual capacity. No report on its opening or cost was found.
Bank of China opened liaison offices (2014), received its establishment permit with 300m USD of capital in May 2016 and its operating licence in December 2017.
A COSCO Pacific-led consortium bought 65% of Kumport (Ambarlı) for 940m USD in 2015, then the largest Chinese FDI in Turkey.

After winning the 2012 tender for 324 Ankara metro cars with a 51% local-content rule, CSR Zhuzhou and MNG Holding built a 110m USD rail vehicle plant in the Sincan industrial zone. The first phase started production in August 2014 and the first vehicle followed that December; work then stopped for about three years and resumed in April 2017 under the name CRRC-MNG.
A Chinese company took 10-year operating rights to a copper site in Arguvan (2012).
ChemChina took control of Pirelli in 2015 (with Türk Pirelli in İzmit); spin-off Prometeon spent 115m USD in İzmit in 2017–20 and planned 40m USD more.
amount_reported: 7,700m USD (global ChemChina–Pirelli deal); Prometeon İzmit: >150m USD 2017–23

summary: Chery set up a wholly owned Turkish sales company in September 2022 and sells directly; in July 2024 it ranked third in monthly car sales. Its Turkey president said feasibility work for local production was under way.

project_name: China Road and Bridge Turkey office
summary: CRBC has a Turkey general manager (2015); later bid for the 1915 Çanakkale Bridge.
China Telecom Europe built a point of presence in Istanbul and signed a cooperation MoU with Türk Telekom International in 2014; the group later set up a wholly owned Turkish subsidiary in Maslak.
A Chinese national co-founded a made-to-measure shirt maker in Sakarya that began exporting (2014).

project_name: Chinese purchases of marble quarries (unnamed buyers)
provinces: Antalya; Burdur; Isparta; Bursa; Muğla; Afyonkarahisar
summary: Exporter associations reported Chinese firms buying and operating marble quarries (about 100 in Antalya, Burdur and Isparta by 2014); buyers are never named.

status_detail: Under construction (about 90% complete, August 2026); production planned for early 2027
holding_entity: Astronergy Europe GmbH (Germany) holds 50% of the cell venture; Chint Electrics (Hong Kong) holds the sales company
summary: Chint's solar arm Astronergy announced a TOPCon cell factory under the HIT-30 programme in April 2025, first put at 500m USD and in July 2025 reported as a 700m USD, 5 GW plant in the Balıkesir organised industrial zone. In November 2025 Alfa Solar and Astronergy's German company were reported to hold 50% each of the project company, with a first phase of 2.5 GW for about 200m USD. In August 2026 Alfa Solar told the stock exchange that construction was about 90% complete, with production planned for the first quarter of 2027.

project_name: Earlier Chinese investment in Mardin OSB (unnamed)
summary: Mardin officials said the OSB had earlier received investment from China (2012).
Sylvania, bought by China's Feilo in 2016, opened a Turkey office in 2017.

investor: Unnamed Chinese partner (75% of Fellow Enerji)
summary: A 2025 newspaper column reports that Fellow Enerji, 75% owned by a Chinese company, makes solar cells in the Gaziantep organised industrial zone with 2.5 GW of cell and 1.6 GW of ingot capacity; the investment started at 120m USD and has reached 150m USD. It exports 80% of output and wants to list on the stock exchange. The Chinese shareholder is not named.

project_name: GCL ND geothermal development (Manisa and Denizli)
investor: GCL (Golden Concord Group); with ND Group
status_detail: Under development (drilling 2017, plant ordered 2018); completion not confirmed
summary: China's Golden Concord Group (GCL) and the Dutch ND Group have worked together since 2015 as GCL ND Enerji to develop geothermal power in Turkey. In 2017 Sinopec's Turkish unit signed an 84.6m USD contract to drill 26 wells for it, and in 2018 it ordered a 12.6 MW plant for Alaşehir, Manisa. The company's own profile speaks of projects in Manisa and Denizli with 730 MW planned and about 1bn USD of investment.
Gate.io started official operations in Turkey in 2022 and named a country manager.

investor: CWT Globelink (CWT, bought by HNA in 2017)
summary: Turkey's Ünimar formed Globelink Ünimar with Singapore's CWT Globelink in 2011; it has warehouses in Istanbul and Bursa and planned one in Gebze. The Singapore parent CWT was bought by HNA's Hong Kong-listed arm in 2017, so the Chinese ownership is indirect and came after the joint venture.

project_name: HNA Group in myTECHNIC and myCARGO
summary: HNA Group and New York's Bravia Capital agreed in November 2010 to acquire a majority stake in myTECHNIC, the aircraft maintenance centre at Sabiha Gökçen Airport; a 2012 report describes HNA as co-owner (the founder holding 40%) and as a partner in myCARGO. The price was not disclosed.

project_name: HNA control of Ingram Micro (Turkey unit)
summary: Turkey's Competition Board cleared HNA's takeover of Ingram Micro, including its Turkish operations (2016).

project_name: HT Solar cell and panel factory (Tuzla)
summary: Chinese state-owned HT Solar (HT-SAAE) has made solar cells and panels in Tuzla, Istanbul, since 2016–17: about 20m USD invested and 600 staff by 2018, with 600 MW of panels a year rising to 1,200 MW by 2021. It bid in YEKA and said it would invest 1bn USD if the next YEKA reached 1 GW.
amount_reported: ≈20m USD invested by 2018 (1,000m USD conditional plan)

summary: Haier began building a factory in Eskişehir OSB in 2019; President Erdoğan opened it in October 2021. The 85m EUR investment covers a dryer plant (40m EUR, 1.5m units a year, operating since January 2021) and a dishwasher plant (45m EUR), with 1,600 jobs. In 2024 Haier added a 70m EUR cooking-appliance factory in Eskişehir (1.2m units a year, over 500 jobs).

Ningbo's Haitian group, selling injection moulding machines in Turkey since 2007, opened a 5,000 m² stock, test and training facility in Velimeşe, Çorlu in July 2018; its machine-tool arm Haitian Precision opened a 1,000 m² application centre in Gebze in September 2023.
Shanghai's Huaming, a maker of transformer tap changers, runs one of its two overseas factories in Turkey; its 2026 Hong Kong listing document dates production there to 2016.

Huawei opened its Ümraniye R&D centre in 2010 (planned >50m USD in 3 years); it reported 120m USD by 2016 and 520m TL over 10 years, and by 2021 some 309m USD invested since 2010 with over 700 engineers.
ICBC agreed in 2014 to buy 75.5% of Tekstilbank for 669m TL, completed in May 2015 (renamed ICBC Turkey), then doubled its capital in 2016.
Mobile game company IGG, founded in Fuzhou and headquartered in Singapore, announced an Istanbul office in October 2018 with a target of about 100 staff and Turkish-language titles.
Shenzhen-based industrial automation maker Inovance runs an Istanbul office with local sales and technical support and exhibits at Turkish trade fairs; no production in Turkey is reported.
Isparta Municipality formed Isparta Gül Ltd (51%) with Chinese partners (49%) for a lithium battery factory (2012).
The Chinese corrugated-board machinery maker serves Turkey, Iran, the Caucasus and Central Asia from an Istanbul facility that trade press dates to 2003.

project_name: Jiangxi Copper stake in Nesko Metal
summary: A consortium led by state-owned Jiangxi Copper bought 50% of Istanbul-based Nesko Metal (Ekin Maden group) for 65m USD in 2014. Nesko is a Turkish company, but its copper mines are in Albania.
KUKA, controlled by China's Midea since 2017, has a Turkey country manager.

Kaishan announced a compressor factory in the İzmir Free Zone in November 2024, started building in July 2025 and opened the roughly 20,000 m² plant in June 2026; it makes screw compressors and equipment for geothermal plants, first for the US market. The zone's chairman put the investment at 1bn USD when it was announced; the opening report gives 20m USD.
amount_reported: 20m USD at opening (1,000m USD announced in 2024)

summary: Kerry Logistics invested in China–Turkey road/rail services (2018) and in November 2019 bought a majority of ASAV Lojistik, one of Turkey's largest air forwarders, with seven offices (five in Istanbul, Bursa and İzmir) and a 452,000 sq ft warehouse in Istanbul. Stake and price were not disclosed.
Li & Fung opened its Istanbul headquarters building in Bahçelievler in 2010 (400 staff), running Europe/North Africa sourcing.

Midea completed its acquisition of Teka Group in 2025; Teka has two plants in Turkey, in İzmir (24,000 m², 2 million units a year, mostly exported) and Çerkezköy, and targets fivefold growth in Turkey in five years. Midea manages regional operations from Turkey, launched Toshiba white goods there in 2026 and is studying production at the İzmir plant; a new factory is still under consideration.

New Hope opened an animal-feed factory in Adana OSB in 2015. A 2021 report puts the investment at about 13m USD and capacity at 200,000 t a year with 80 staff, and says the company plans to raise capacity and build further plants, first in Manisa.
State-owned scanner maker Nuctech supplies airports and customs in Turkey through a local office; in 2023 it said it had served the Turkish market for 21 years.

The Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels, owner and operator, with its local partners Doğuş and Bilgili, announced the opening of the 177-room Peninsula Istanbul at Galataport, Karaköy, for 14 February 2023; the investment was reported at 300m EUR, with 400 staff at opening.

status_detail: Acquired 47% (2011); shares sold in the 2021 IPO
holding_entity: PineBridge Eurasia Financial Investments S.à r.l.
summary: PineBridge, the former AIG asset manager owned by Hong Kong's Pacific Century Group from 2010, bought 47% of Ulusal Faktoring through a Luxembourg vehicle in 2011. Turkish press presents it as the buyer of the American insurer AIG's fund-management arm. PineBridge sold shares when the company went public in November 2021.

PowerChina opened its Eurasia regional headquarters, covering 63 countries, in Istanbul on 23 May 2017. In 2022 it was reported to have nine projects under construction in Turkey (five hydropower stations and four thermal power projects) with contracts worth up to 3bn USD.

project_name: Qitaihe LongCoal purchase of Polyak Eynez shares (Kınık coal mine)
summary: The Turkish subsidiary of Heilongjiang's Qitaihe LongCoal bought Fina Holding's shares in Polyak Eynez, the company behind the Eynez underground coal mine in Kınık. Stake and price were not disclosed; the source is the announcement of the seller's law firm.
Riot Games, majority-owned by Tencent since 2011, opened a direct Turkey office in 2012.
State Power Investment Corp.'s first solar investment in Turkey, the Adıyaman photovoltaic project, was connected to the grid in December 2017 and had generated 71.6 GWh by early 2022.

project_name: Shanghai Electric's EMBA Hunutlu power plant
summary: A Shanghai Electric Power-led consortium signed contracts in 2018 for the 1,320 MW EMBA Hunutlu plant; ministers called it one of China's largest direct investments in Turkey.

investment_type: Hotel partnership (management; shareholder in the owning company)
holding_entity: Shangri-La shareholder entity registered in Luxembourg
summary: Shangri-La agreed with Tanrıverdi Holding in 2010 on a hotel in the former tobacco warehouse in Beşiktaş, reported as a 250m USD project; it opened in May 2013 with 186 rooms. Press reports describe Shangri-La as the operator, while the trade registry lists it as a shareholder of the owning company through Luxembourg.

Talks on producing Sinovac in Turkey were reported in September 2021 and the Competition Board cleared a joint venture of Sinovac and Alagöz Holding that November. The KeyVac plant in Ankara, reported as a 100m USD investment with 29,000 m² and capacity for 30 million doses a year, opened in November 2023 as Sinovac's first plant outside China; it is to make hepatitis A vaccine.

status_detail: Operating (module and pack production since March 2023)
summary: Togg chose Farasis in 2020; their JV Siro will make battery cells and modules in Gemlik (15 GWh), with project-based state aid from 2021.
TECNO invested 25–35m USD in a Pendik plant and began production in 2021, targeting about 1,000 jobs.

project_name: TISCO chrome mines and Kop Krom concentrator
investor: TISCO (Taiyuan Iron & Steel); Shanxi Jinzhong Wanbang; with CVK Group
investment_type: Investment in mining companies + concentration plant
summary: State-owned stainless steel maker TISCO was reported in 2009 to have invested about 300m USD in three Turkish mining companies with 15 chrome licences. With Jinzhong Wanbang and CVK Group it built the Kop Krom ore concentration plant on Kop mountain, ready for trial production at the end of August 2010 (planned output 150,000 t, 508 jobs).

project_name: TP-Link Turkey office and production plan
status_detail: Office operating since 2010; production plan not confirmed
holding_entity: TP-Link Technologies (SG); direct from China at founding
summary: TP-Link opened its Turkey office in Istanbul at the end of 2010 and moved to a 1,200 m² office with 40 staff by 2013. In December 2020 its deputy country manager announced a plan to open a production facility in Turkey by 2022; no report of its realisation was found.

Temu, launched in Turkey in 2024, registered a local company and opened an Istanbul office in 2025, began hiring and signed up Turkish sellers and logistics partners. After a Competition Authority raid and the end of the 30 EUR customs exemption it stopped cross-border sales in January 2026 and now lists only Turkey-based sellers.

project_name: Texhong yarn plant in Balıkesir OSB
summary: A Chinese yarn maker (Texhong) planned a 70–150m USD plant; Balıkesir OSB allocated land in 2013.
Xiaomi and Salcomp (owned by China's Luxshare) opened a 30m USD plant in Avcılar in March 2021 (5m phones/yr, 2,000 jobs).
Alkut set up Urumçi Tarım AŞ in Ankara for a >100m USD thermal health and herbal medicine investment (2015).

status_detail: Company says local production began in March 2026
summary: Yadea said in April 2026 that it is entering Turkey through its own operations, started localised production in March 2026 and is building a sales and service network. The only source is a company press release; the site and ownership of the production are not given.

Injection moulding machine maker Yizumi opened a technology centre in Silivri in May 2025, its first investment in Turkey, with demonstration machines, training, a local engineering team and a spare parts depot.
ZTE bought 48.04% of Netaş from OEP for 101.3m USD (signed Dec 2016, closed Jul 2017), then announced new investments and local production.

project_name: ZTT cable plants and Demirer Kablo acquisition
summary: ZTT announced 110m USD of cable investments (2018) and bought Demirer Kablo in Bilecik for 66.7m USD.
Zoomlion, previously sold in Turkey through a distributor, set up its own Istanbul subsidiary in 2018 and has built a network of branches and parts depots; no Turkish factory is reported.

holding_entity: Winning Concept (Hong Kong) holds the Turkish sales company
summary: vivo began production at a 20m USD, 12,000 m² plant in Gebze Güzeller OSB in August 2021 (up to 5m phones a year, over 2,000 jobs planned within three years); since 2024 it also makes V-series Lite models there.

project_name: Şırnak coal plant – Chinese builder with 10% stake
summary: Galata Enerji signed a 355m USD EPC contract with CMEC (2010); in 2012 it said the Chinese builder had been given a 10% partnership.
Bloomberg reported a Chinese bank was interested in DenizBank (2018); Emirates NBD bought it.

project_name: Chinese firms seeking Turkish pasta makers
summary: Chinese firms were reported to be in talks to buy Turkish pasta makers (2017).
Reports in 2018 said a Chinese company (Tatwah) was in talks for the 55% Türk Telekom stake held by lenders.

project_name: Energy group in talks with Chinese buyers (2015)
summary: A 2015 article said a large Turkish energy group was negotiating to sell its power companies to Chinese investors.
Sabancı said in 2016 there was no decision on reported Enerjisa share sales to Chinese investors.

project_name: ICBC plan to take over HSBC Turkey branches
summary: A 2015 press report said ICBC planned to take over 277 HSBC Turkey branches.
